design_decisions.question: Parse Cargo.lock with a general TOML library, or a dedicated parser?
design_decisions.decision: Dedicated minimal parser for exactly Cargo.lock's own stable, machine-generated subset and exactly the bounded Cargo.toml dependency-table shapes this workspace's manifests use. Avoids adding a new crate to census dependencies that would itself immediately need census (a bootstrap circularity), matching the same 'avoid the general tool, use the bounded real shape' discipline already used for syn/quote over regex for Rust source.

design_decisions.question: Does Cargo.lock alone give the full transitive closure?
design_decisions.decision: Yes -- Cargo.lock is Cargo's own already-fully-resolved transitive dependency graph (each [[package]] entry lists its own resolved dependencies), so pure static parsing (never cargo tree/cargo metadata execution, matching the ingestion-is-not-execution security boundary) yields complete closure for this ecosystem without a separate resolution algorithm.

design_decisions.question: What DependencyKind for a transitive edge between two external (non-workspace) packages, whose own manifest this parser never reads?
design_decisions.decision: kind: Option<DependencyKind> = None -- never defaulted to Runtime by assumption. Only a workspace member's own directly-read Cargo.toml ever produces Some(kind). This is the same 'never claim a fact this extractor cannot prove from the input it actually read' discipline as CallDispatchKind::Unresolved/DataFlowResolution::Unresolved.

design_decisions.question: How to handle an ambiguous lockfile reference (multiple resolved versions sharing one name)?
design_decisions.decision: Report as a closure-blocking reference (alongside genuine dangling references) rather than guess which version, since this parser does not yet read Cargo.lock's 'name version' disambiguated array-entry form. Zero real occurrences in this workspace's own lockfile (verified), so this is a named, tested, not-yet-exercised gap rather than a live one.
